
=== session 2026-11-11T07:03:50Z ===
$ kiro-cli chat --output-format stream-json --v3 --mode spec --trust-all-tools --trust-workspace --model claude-opus-5.5 "$(cat docs/kiro-evidence/prompts/12-spec-kitchen-mcp.md)"
--- prompt ---
Write the spec `kitchen-mcp` in .kiro/specs/kitchen-mcp/: requirements.md, then design.md, then tasks.md. No code in this session.

The scheduler is deterministic core code, so any agent should be able to use it as a tool. This spec adds an MCP server (stdio) in src/mcp that exposes the core and nothing else, registers it in .kiro/settings/mcp.json for this workspace, and uses it during development: Kiro itself can then answer "schedule the Sunday roast with one burner" or "does every sample still land within its holds after this change" by calling the real scheduler instead of reasoning about it. Read the steering (structure.md names the tools: check_plan, schedule_plan, rebuild_plan, export_dinnerfile, import_dinnerfile; product.md: no model calls here), the specs recipe-graph, scheduler, rebuild and dinnerfile (exact core signatures), and the installed @modelcontextprotocol/sdk version's real API (look in node_modules before fixing signatures). Follow the format of the earlier specs.

Scope:
- Tools with zod input schemas and structured results: check_plan(plan) -> issues; schedule_plan(plan, kitchen) -> schedule or typed error; rebuild_plan(schedule, progress, now) -> rebuilt or typed error; export_dinnerfile(plan, options?) -> text; import_dinnerfile(text) -> plan or line-numbered errors; plus list_samples() and get_sample(id) -> the recorded plan, so an agent has something to schedule without pasting JSON. Each tool also returns a short human-readable text block (for schedule_plan: the plan list as text, one line per step with relative minutes, lanes and marks).
- Errors are tool results with isError, never thrown protocol errors, and never contain stack traces.
- No network, no file writes, no environment access beyond reading samples/ and recordings/ relative to the package root.
- `npm run mcp` starts it from source with tsx; the build emits dist/mcp/index.js; .kiro/settings/mcp.json registers it for this workspace under the name `make-dinner`.
- Tests: in-process tests using the SDK's in-memory transport pair (client and server linked without a process) for every tool, success and error; one test that spawns the built server over stdio, lists the tools and calls schedule_plan on a sample.
- A custom agent .kiro/agents/taster.json that uses only this MCP server and read access: given a sample id or a plan, it schedules it under two or three kitchens and reports, as a cook would read it, anything odd (a dish waiting past its hold, a cook double-booked according to the text, a start time that makes no sense), quoting the tool results. Its config and a recorded run are part of the tasks.
- The README section that tells a user how to add the server to their own MCP client.

Keep tasks.md to about 12 to 16 sub-tasks.

Length: this is a thin adapter over core. Aim for requirements.md under 110 lines, design.md under 260 lines and tasks.md under 130 lines. Read only what you need: the core index.ts exports, the Schedule, Progress and Dinnerfile types, and the MCP SDK's server and in-memory transport typings. Do not run exploratory scripts beyond confirming the SDK's import paths.

            }
            return parseResult.data;
        }
        /**
         * Validates tool output against the tool's output schema.
         */
        async validateToolOutput(tool, result, toolName) {
            if (!tool.outputSchema) {
                return;
            }
            // Only validate CallToolResult, not CreateTaskResult
            if (!('content' in result)) {
                return;
            }
            if (result.isError) {
                return;
            }
            if (!result.structuredContent) {
                throw new McpError(ErrorCode.InvalidParams, `Output validation error: Tool ${toolName} has an output schema but no structured content was provided`);
            }
            // if the tool has an output schema, validate structured content
            const outputObj = normalizeObjectSchema(tool.outputSchema);
            const parseResult = await safeParseAsync(outputObj, result.structuredContent);
            if (!parseResult.success) {
                const error = 'error' in parseResult ? parseResult.error : 'Unknown error';
                const errorMessage = getParseErrorMessage(error);
                throw new McpError(ErrorCode.InvalidParams, `Output validation error: Invalid structured content for tool ${toolName}: ${errorMessage}`);
            }
        }

    exit 0

[tool:execute] $ cd node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk && sed -n 480,510p dist/esm/client/index.js
    … (1 earlier lines not shown)
            if (this.isToolTaskRequired(params.name)) {
                throw new McpError(ErrorCode.InvalidRequest, `Tool "${params.name}" requires task-based execution. Use client.experimental.tasks.callToolStream() instead.`);
            }
            const result = await this.request({ method: 'tools/call', params }, resultSchema, options);
            // Check if the tool has an outputSchema
            const validator = this.getToolOutputValidator(params.name);
            if (validator) {
                // If tool has outputSchema, it MUST return structuredContent (unless it's an error)
                if (!result.structuredContent && !result.isError) {
                    throw new McpError(ErrorCode.InvalidRequest, `Tool ${params.name} has an output schema but did not return structured content`);
                }
                // Only validate structured content if present (not when there's an error)
                if (result.structuredContent) {
                    try {
                        // Validate the structured content against the schema
                        const validationResult = validator(result.structuredContent);
                        if (!validationResult.valid) {
                            throw new McpError(ErrorCode.InvalidParams, `Structured content does not match the tool's output schema: ${validationResult.errorMessage}`);
                        }
                    }
                    catch (error) {
                        if (error instanceof McpError) {
                            throw error;
                        }
                        throw new McpError(ErrorCode.InvalidParams, `Failed to validate structured content: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`);
                    }
                }
            }
            return result;
        }

I've written the `kitchen-mcp` spec as three files in `.kiro/specs/kitchen-mcp/`. No code was written. All three are under your length limits: requirements.md is 109 lines, design.md 259 and tasks.md 129. `tasks.md` has 16 sub-tasks; `scripts/hooks/tasks-lint.sh` and `npx prettier --check .kiro/specs/kitchen-mcp/` both pass on it. Those are the only checks I ran; no tests were run, because there is no code yet.

Reading the installed SDK (1.32.2) changed four parts of the design:

- **Error results:** the SDK client checks `structuredContent` against the tool's success schema even when `isError` is set. So a tool error carries no `structuredContent`. It returns two text blocks instead: a plain-English message, then a JSON block with `{ error: { code, message, ...details } }`.
- **Thrown errors:** the SDK catches every throw in `tools/call` (unknown tool, input validation, input-size limit) and turns it into an `isError` result. So no protocol error ever reaches the agent.
- **Input schemas:** the tools advertise the real core schemas, so the SDK rejects badly shaped arguments with its own "Input validation error" message before our code runs. `check_plan` takes any value, so an agent can still get a broken plan's problems one by one.
- **Success results:** each success returns `structuredContent` plus two text blocks, the readable summary and the JSON. That way a client that ignores `structuredContent` can still pass a schedule on to `rebuild_plan`.

The design also includes:
- the plan-list text worked out by hand for the Sunday roast example, line by line;
- the table of error codes and messages;
- the lint rules that block network, file writes and `process.env` in `src/mcp`;
- the taster's three kitchens (the sample's suggested one, one burner, one oven and one cook) and its prompt.

Things that changed while I worked, or that you need to know:

- **Another session is editing the same tree.** At the start, `samples/index.json` and `src/server/parse/` didn't exist. They now do, uncommitted, from what looks like a recipe-reader implementation session. That session moved `SampleEntrySchema` into `src/core/api.ts`. The design follows that: `src/mcp` imports `SampleEntrySchema` from core, and copies `SampleIndexSchema` and `RecordingSchema`, because `src/mcp` may not import from `src/server`. A parity test keeps the copies equal. `recordings/` still doesn't exist.
- **Three tasks need the recordings,** which only you can make with `npm run record`: T3.2 (the stdio test), the by-hand part of T3.3 and T4.2 (the recorded taster run).
- **T4.2 is yours to run,** because only `scripts/kiro-run.sh` may write to `docs/kiro-evidence/`. Prompt number 17 is already used by the plan-ui prompts, so the design asks you to pick the next free number.
- **The `invalid_now` message gives no numbers.** `AXIS_MIN` and `REBUILD_LIMITS` aren't exported from `src/core/index.ts`, and this spec doesn't change core.
- **After a change to `src/core`,** reconnect `make-dinner` from Kiro's MCP panel before asking whether every sample still lands within its holds. The server runs from source and doesn't reload itself.

Questions for you, listed at the end of `design.md`:
1. Should `SampleIndexSchema` and `RecordingSchema` move into `src/core/api.ts` next to `SampleEntrySchema`? Then nothing needs copying.
2. Does Kiro start workspace MCP servers from the workspace root? The `mcp.json` entry uses the relative path `src/mcp/index.ts`; T3.3 checks this by hand.
3. Do `tools: ["read", "@make-dinner"]` and `includeMcpJson: true` really keep your user-level MCP servers away from the taster? T4.1 checks the Kiro agent docs before writing the file.
